standard.title: Create informative and imaginative texts
standard.description: create spoken, written and multimodal informative and imaginative texts, using vocabulary, expressions, sentence structures, textual conventions and appropriate characters and/or Pinyin, to suit purpose and audience
standard.prior_knowledge: Students entering at Y7-8 can produce spoken and written target language in familiar registers from home exposure. They may have informal literacy skills of varying depth. They have not yet created extended texts using academic vocabulary, textual conventions, and deliberate stylistic choices for a range of purposes and audiences in a school context.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students create spoken, written and multimodal informative and imaginative texts using vocabulary, expressions, sentence structures and textual conventions appropriate to purpose and audience.

nodes.label: Informative texts for real purposes
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create informative texts — presentations, posters, brochures, newsletters — using appropriate textual conventions and supporting visual elements.
nodes.minimum_width: Create at least one informative text using appropriate target language textual conventions and at least one supporting visual element.
nodes.typical_width: Create digital presentations with sound, voice and music; produce posters and brochures for cultural events; write journal entries and school newsletter contributions; develop procedural texts such as recipes, tutorials and instruction guides; create subtitles and captions for video.
wider: Create an informative text for a real external audience — evaluate its effectiveness with the intended audience and revise
Compare informative text conventions in the target language with English equivalents — identify differences in structure, visual convention and audience address
nodes.hinge_reason: Informative text creation with appropriate conventions is the prerequisite for all academic text production at this level. Entry students with strong oral skills but limited formal writing experience need this foundation before extended or imaginative text production.

response_modes.reason: Informative text conventions require repeated production practice across different formats. Regular creation tasks with explicit attention to genre conventions build the formal text production skills the descriptor requires.

success_criteria: Creates an informative text using appropriate target language textual conventions
Includes at least one supporting visual element used purposefully

nodes.label: Imaginative and creative texts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create imaginative texts — stories, songs, role-plays, cultural narratives — using descriptive language, cultural references, and deliberate creative choices.
nodes.minimum_width: Create at least one imaginative text demonstrating at least one deliberate creative choice (language, structure, cultural reference, or performance element).
nodes.typical_width: Create stories about Chinese-speaking Australians; compose songs, jingles or video clips; write and perform role-plays using cultural stories; create original stories using common expressions or traditional literary idioms; produce bilingual creative texts.
wider: Create an imaginative text that draws on a specific target language literary or cultural tradition — explain the creative choices made and how they reflect that tradition
Produce an imaginative text for a real community audience — performing or publishing for Chinese-speaking community members

response_modes.reason: Imaginative text creation requires encounter with varied creative forms — stories, songs, role-plays, videos — before students can make independent genre and format choices. Varied creative tasks build the repertoire of forms available for deliberate selection.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Background language learner entry students bring cultural knowledge — stories, songs, community practices — that can enrich creative text production. Width investment in tasks that draw on this cultural knowledge produces authentic, culturally grounded creative work.
success_criteria: Creates an imaginative text with at least one deliberate creative choice
Demonstrates cultural knowledge through at least one reference, convention or language choice in the text

nodes.label: Audience-aware multimodal production
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create multimodal texts combining spoken, written and visual elements, making deliberate production choices appropriate to purpose and audience.
nodes.minimum_width: Create a multimodal text combining at least two modes with at least one deliberate production choice justified by audience or purpose.
nodes.typical_width: Create multimodal texts combining text, image, sound and performance; adapt language for purpose and audience; produce texts depicting intercultural experiences; create works for Chinese-speaking community audiences; develop drafting and revision skills in own multimodal production.
wider: Create a multimodal text for a specifically defined audience — evaluate its effectiveness with that audience and revise based on feedback
Reflect on the production choices made — explain how each mode contributes to meaning and why the combination is more effective than a single mode

response_modes.reason: Audience-aware multimodal production integrates informative text skills (node 1) and imaginative text creation (node 2) into a full production task. The teaching investment is in creating genuine audience conditions — real presentations, real community audiences — where production choices carry communicative weight.

success_criteria: Creates a multimodal text combining at least two modes
Demonstrates at least one deliberate production choice appropriate to audience or purpose
